articles.summary: The US has reintroduced a naval blockade of Iranian ports, following allegations of Iranian attacks on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. The blockade was in place between 13 April and 18 June, with the US redirecting more than 140 vessels and disabling nine ships during this period. It is unclear if this particular vessel, Belma, changed its course after being warned about its potential violations. The sanctions were lifted after a ceasefire deal was reached in June, and experts estimate that Iran exported at least 74 million barrels of oil worth up to $6bn before they were reimposed.
articles.shortSummary: The US fired Hellfire missiles at a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, violating multiple warnings and prompting a new Iran blockade.

articles.summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry has stated that the US must stop using military pressure against Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway that Iran closed in response to a US-Israeli military campaign in February. The US imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports, escalating a standoff over the strategic waterway. Iran has laid out a series of conditions for reopening the strait, including compensation for war damage, the lifting of sanctions, the release of frozen Iranian funds, and a permanent end to hostilities against Iran and its regional allies. The disruption to Hormuez has put pressure on global energy markets, with oil prices rising nearly 3% amid uncertainty over negotiations.
articles.shortSummary: Iran's Foreign Ministry says Washington must stop using military force to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, despite Tehran's conditions for reopening it.

articles.summary: Iran has offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within a seven-day period if the US ends its blockade and military pressure campaign, according to a report. The offer was made as both the US and Iranian leaders converge on New York City for the United Nations General Assembly. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio suggested a potential meeting between President Trump and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, who is seen as a more moderate figure within Iranian leadership. Despite this, there are no indications that a Pezshkian-Trump powwow will occur on the sidelines of the UNGA. Despite Iran's efforts, US officials have insisted that they are getting oil through the Strait Hormz by using routes close to the shores of Oman.
articles.shortSummary: Iran offers to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the US ends its blockade and military pressure, aiming for peace talks with Iran's leaders at the UNGA.

articles.summary: US forces boarded a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz amid a naval blockade as President Donald Trump mulls his next move on Iran. The move was delayed due to a diminished stockpile of Patriot antimissile interceptors, but still promised major punishment for Tehran and its Houthi puppets. Since the blockade was reinstated, 12 commercial vessels have been redirected, two disabled, and two boarded. The Houthis have also claimed to have attacked several Saudi Arabian vessels in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key trade waterway linking the Red Sea to Europe. Meanwhile, daily US airstrikes on Iran have stopped after two weeks of intense bombing. Peace talks have been resumed as Washington and Tehran try to avoid all-out war. There are fears that Iran's new Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei is more determined to develop a nuclear bomb than his late father, which could undermine any peace agreement given his commitment to long-term denuclearisation.
articles.shortSummary: US forces boarded a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz amid a blockade of Iran, with President Donald Trump considering a major military response.

Once the scheme is operational, food waste will be recycled into clean energy and fertiliser.

articles.summary: The United States and Iran have escalated into a conflict, with President Donald Trump reinstating a naval blockade against ships travelling to and from Iranian ports. The United States will charge cargo ships a 20% fee or any costs deemed necessary to provide safety and security to these areas. The blockade will only prevent Iran's ships and its customers from leaving the waterway, while other countries should have fair and open access. This follows the US and Israel's initial strikes against Iran in February, which resulted in Tehran restricting access to the strategically important Strait of Hormuz. The strait is a key shipping route for global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies and represents a major threat to energy markets.
articles.shortSummary: President Donald Trump has reinstated a naval blockade of Iran's ships in the Strait of Hormuz, amid escalating conflict and trade tensions.

articles.summary: The US military has maintained the Strait of Hormuz open to commercial shipping, despite an ongoing blockade on Iranian maritime trade and attacks by Iran's military on commercial ships. US Navy Captain Tim Hawkins, a spokesperson for US Central Command (CENTCOM), stated that traffic through the strait "continues to flow" and denied Iran controls the waterway. Hawkins also defended US military operations in the region against civilian casualties and damage to civilian infrastructure. The comments come amid heightened tensions over shipping through the vital waterway, a critical route for global energy supplies.
articles.shortSummary: The US military claims the Strait of Hormuz remains open to commercial shipping despite an ongoing Iranian blockade, emphasizing ongoing operations and ongoing monitoring of shipping lanes.

The US has announced it will resume a blockade on Iranian oil exports and potentially charge ships crossing Hormud with American military protection. The country also carried out another round of bombing against Iran. These attacks have pushed oil prices up by almost 14% so far this week. Despite this, crude markets remain low and fuel markets are strong, indicating a continued risk to prices. articles.summary: Two sailors are missing and 23 others have been rescued following an attack on an oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, Oman. The Panama-flagged El Gaia was being towed to an Omani port after a fire broke out in its engine room. Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed that the tanker hit naval mines and caught fire while passing through a restricted and unsafe route. However, the US military denied this, claiming the tanker was hit by an Iranian missile last month and again by a drone over the weekend. The Strait of Haormuz has been effectively closed due to Iranian missile and drone attacks on commercial vessels and a US naval blockade of Iranian ports. The International Maritime Organization has reported at least 22 seafarers killed in 79 incidents in the region since the start of the US and Israel's war with Iran.
articles.shortSummary: Two sailors are missing and 23 are rescued after an oil tanker El Gaia was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz by Iran, which has repeatedly targeted vessels.

This follows a 10 consecutive night of US airstrikes that have not deterred Tehran from loosening its grip on the straits, a vital route for global energy supplies. articles.title: Saudi Arabia Resumes Oil Shipments Through Strait of Hormuz

articles.summary: Saudi Arabia has resumed oil loading from the Strait of Hormuz, with more tankers waiting to load as the state energy giant offers spot heavy crude cargoes. The world's top oil exporter, Saudi Aramco, had halted sales for weeks due to attacks on its tanker fleet during the U.S.-Iran conflict. The resumption of exports could help ease the shortage of heavier grades that produce more residue fuel, which can be used to refuel ships or processed further at refineries to yield higher-quality fuels. However, Saudi oil exports remain curtailed due to a blockade by the Yemeni Houthis in the Red Sea. The country has also offered additional crude cagoes for loading from Egypt's Mediterranean port of Sidi Kerir, but these volumes are not reaching the preblockade level.
articles.shortSummary: Saudi Aramco resumed oil loading from inside the Strait of Hormuz, offering heavy crude cargoes to Asian refiners, but ongoing curbs on Saudi exports continue.

articles.summary: Shipping traffic in the Strait of Hormuz has decreased sharply due to the Iran war, which has escalated and threatens to worsen a worldwide crude shortage. Oil data company Kpler reported that it counted 30 verified tanker crossings over a three-day period, marking a 72% drop from the previous two weeks. Gas prices in the United States topped $4 per gallon as oil costs rose due to increased tensions in the Gulf. The Iran war resulted in the closure of the Strait Hormz, the maritime trading route that supplies about one-fifth of global oil supply. The U.S. resumed its naval blockade of the strait last week, reversing a key commitment made as part of the agreement. Brent crude futures, the benchmark index for worldwide trading, rose to nearly $89 a barrel on Monday, marking crude prices close to their highest level since June 15.
articles.shortSummary: Oil prices rose as shipping traffic in the Strait of Hormuz declined sharply amid escalating tensions between Iran and its allies, raising concerns about global crude shortages.

articles.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has reportedly fired on at least two commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz, threatening to unravel a cease-fire agreement reached less than three weeks ago. The Al Rekayyat, an LNG vessel belonging to Qatar's state-owned shipping company, was also damaged while leaving the strait. Both ships were transiting without their transponders active. The Joint Maritime Information Center, a multinational naval body, raised regional shipping risk from substantial to severe, citing evidence Iran is determined to extend its influence over major transit corridors in the waterway. State television in Tehran suggested Iranian forces were behind the strike, though the government did not formally claim responsibility. The incidents triggered a sharp increase in oil prices and demand for greater control over shipping routes and tolls.
articles.shortSummary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps attacked Qatari LNG tanker and Saudi oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, threatening a cease-fire agreement and disrupting diplomatic efforts.

articles.summary: The US has fired on an oil tanker attempting to reach Kharg Island in the strait of Hormuz, as part of its blockade on Iranian ports. This comes as Tehran came under attack for the first time in this latest round of strikes. The US disabled an unladen oil tanker and fired Hellfire missiles into its smokestack after it ignored multiple warnings. The Iranian government responded with attacks on Bahrain and Kuwait. The recent attacks have reportedly killed over 35 people and wounded over 300 others. Despite this, the US has reimposed its naval blockade on Iran and threatened to halt all energy exports from the Middle East. Oil prices have continued to rise throughout this period, with Brent crude oil trading at above $85 a barrel, more than 15% higher than the price before the war.
articles.shortSummary: The US has disabled an oil tanker in the strait of Hormuz, amid escalating attacks on Iranian ports and targets in Tehran.

articles.title: Iran and Oman edge towards deal on Strait of Hormuz
articles.description: Interim proposal on managing shipping is first hint of diplomatic progress to reopen the waterway in weeks
articles.content: Iran and Oman have edged towards an interim agreement on managing shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, the first hint of diplomatic progress in weeks as mediators seek to defuse the battle over the ... [4542 symbols]
articles.summary: Iran and Oman are close to an interim agreement on managing shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, the first hint of diplomatic progress in weeks. The parties have discussed a "proposed framework" to establish a temporary corridor for ships to move through the strait and implement a project to demine the waterway. This includes lifting a naval blockade on Iranian ports and reinstating a waiver to allow Iran to sell oil. Negotiations between Iran and Oman have been ongoing since a June memorandum of understanding between Washington and Tehran collapsed last month. The deal is hoped to pave a path for the US and Iran to return to the MoU, which originally allowed shipping to return without paying fees while they were in talks on a final settlement.
articles.shortSummary: Iran and Oman are negotiating a provisional deal to manage shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, amid ongoing diplomatic efforts to defuse the conflict.
